t:
There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for the purposes of this Act, but appropriations for public works projects authorized by titles I, II, III, IV, and V shall not exceed—

    (1) 
for title I: Inside the United States, $57,219,000; Outside the United States, $36,141,000; section 102, $33,000,000; or a total of $126,360,000.
 
    (2) 
for title II: Inside the United States, $114,138,000; Outside the United States, $9,948,000; section 202, $13,788,000; or a total of $137,874,000.
 
    (3) 
for title III: Inside the United States, $107,098,000; Outside the United States, $14,091,000; section 302, $76,825,000; or a total of $198,014,000.
 
    (4) 
for title IV: a total of $5,875,000.
 
    (5) 
for title V: Military Family Housing, a total of $511,196,000.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations and sets dollar ceilings for military public works projects under several titles. It contains no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no real tempting contrary reading; it is purely a funding limitation.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for the purposes of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section solely establishes funding limits and authorizes appropriations for various titles of the Act. It does not contain any language requiring consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text is purely financial and administrative.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for the purposes of this Act, but appropriations for public works projects authorized by titles I, II, III, IV, and V shall not exceed—

opus.w: The section authorizes appropriations and caps how much can be spent on public works projects under titles I through V. It does not provide for consultation, comment periods, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or lawsuits by anyone outside the federal government. The phrase "public works projects" may sound like outside involvement, but it only describes what the money is for and involves no outside party.
opus.b: This section only authorizes appropriations and sets dollar caps. The one tempting hook is "public works projects," which might suggest local involvement. But nothing here has any outside party consulting, commenting, sitting on a board, or suing over a federal decision. It is like Example 1, a pure funding provision.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely authorizes appropriations and sets spending limits for various titles of the Act. It does not contain any language requiring consultation, public comment, hearings, or coordination with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making decisions. The mention of 'public works' describes the type of project funded, not a participatory process required by this specific text.
qwen_chat.s: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for the purposes of this Act, but appropriations for public works projects authorized by titles I, II, III, IV, and V shall not exceed—
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "public works," there is an implicit requirement for public participation in the planning or execution of those works. However, the text itself only lists dollar amounts and does not mandate any specific participatory process (like hearings or comments) for the appropriation or the projects. The definition requires explicit statutory language mandating consultation, comment periods, or advisory bodies involving outsiders. This section is purely an authorization of appropriations.
